summary: A downward cancellation wand hitting a magical trap reaches zap.c:zap_map, which first calls maybe_explode_trap to explode the trap for 20+d(3,6), delete it and redraw its square. The JS zap_map path omits that call, so the beam reaches its later continuation without the trap explosion; the first recorded RNG and screen divergence is reported at step 280. The helper and caller belong to the reserved zap_map scope in B’s active Castle pass-tune delivery.

source.branch: A cancellation wand or spell hits an undestroyable portal trap or a magical trap. Undestroyable traps display the shield effect and can teach the wand when visible; other magical traps explode for 20+d(3,6), are deleted, redrawn, and teach the wand when visible. Ordinary non-magical traps and non-cancellation objects leave this helper without effects.
callers: zap.c:zap_map calls maybe_explode_trap(ttmp,obj,&learn_it) before refreshing ttmp and before the downward engraving switch.
js/zap.js:zap_map is already reached from js/zap.js:bhit and js/zap.js:zap_updown; adding the call requires editing zap_map, which B currently reserves as source:zap.c:zap_map.
dependencies: include/trap.h:undestroyable_trap and is_magical_trap classification macros are already represented by js/const.js.
zap.c:explode handles the trap blast; js/explode.js exports the existing asynchronous explode implementation.
display.c:shieldeff and newsym and vision.c:cansee have existing JavaScript implementations.
trap.c:deltrap and zap.c:learnwand have existing JavaScript implementations.

evidence: challenges/manifests/v59.json sourcePointers identify zap.c:maybe_explode_trap (3594-3627) -> explode(20+d(3,6)), deltrap, and zap_map caller at line 3642.

Read upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/zap.c:maybe_explode_trap (3594-3623): only cancellation wand/spell types enter; undestroyable traps may shield and teach; magical traps call explode with -WAN_CANCELLATION, physical damage 20+d(3,6), TRAP_EXPLODE and EXPL_MAGICAL, then delete and redraw the trap; visibility sets the learn_it output.

C nethack-c/upstream/src/zap.c:zap_map (3625 onward) calls maybe_explode_trap before its direction/engraving switch and reacquires the trap with t_at because it may have been removed. The JavaScript js/zap.js:zap_map currently starts with the WAN_PROBING branch, then returns for upward zaps or processes only selected downward engravings; it has no cancellation-trap helper call.

The saved v59 case contains a downward cancellation-zap sequence at input steps 278-280; at step 280, C random call 2309 is d(3,6)=7 from maybe_explode_trap(zap.c:3616), while JavaScript consumes rn2(5)=3, and the next screen differs at row 0 column 0. A replay at accepted worker base 51b2152ddf36e693950fc7cc924d325e0132ffcf reproduces that exact first divergence with 280 of 309 screens matching.

Implementation requires changing js/zap.js:zap_map to call the helper before its existing partial arms. The shared ledger currently reserves source:zap.c:zap_map for B’s v58 Castle pass-tune task, so this worker cannot claim or edit the caller until Root resolves the overlap.
